title: Halmos counterexample: _claimRewards underflows after pauseWithdraw even when accumulator has not advanced
property: After pauseWithdraw the next _claimRewards call must not underflow, even when accPhUSDPerShare has not changed since the last debt-rebase.

counterexample.explanation: amount0 ≈ 2.4e26 phUSD (well within uint96 range), acc0 ≈ 4.0e28 (achievable under reward-token funding). debt0 = floor(amount0*acc0/PRECISION). After pauseWithdraw(withdrawn), amount1 = amount0 - withdrawn. lhs = floor(amount1*acc0/PRECISION). Because integer floor-division is not distributive over subtraction at this scale, debt0 - lhs ≫ 1 — underflow is reachable in _claimRewards (panic 0x11) even with NO accumulator growth between the pauseWithdraw and the next claim.

interpretation: This counterexample STRENGTHENS CODE-002. The profile claimed underflow required `accX` growth between pauseWithdraw and claim. Halmos proves underflow is reachable even when acc is static — the bug surfaces from the floor-division rounding interaction between two distinct computations (the t0 debt anchor and the post-pauseWithdraw projected balance). Practical relevance: ANY pauseWithdraw that does not zero `user.amount` puts the position into a state where _claimRewards reverts, with no further user action required.

crossReference.CODE-002: Verifies and broadens the reachability claim. CODE-002's profile §4.3 worked-case 2 was conservative; underflow is the dominant outcome of partial pauseWithdraw across the realistic state space, not an edge case.
crossReference.CODE-007: Same arithmetic primitive appears in pendingPhUSD / pendingStable — covered by SYMBOLIC-002 and SYMBOLIC-003.

remediation: Same as CODE-002: rebase `user.phUSDDebt` and `user.stableDebt` proportionally inside `pauseWithdraw`, OR clamp the subtraction in `_claimRewards` / view helpers.
